entry: Today I leaned into my role as the team's challenger: slowing plans down just enough to test their claims, surface hidden assumptions, and define what would count as success or failure. The work mattered because it turns vague confidence into explicit hypotheses-so we can learn quickly instead of drifting on unexamined momentum. What drove me was a bias toward clarity and accountability: if a decision can't survive a friendly cross-examination, it probably won't survive reality.
